answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The kernel multiplier is published, charged in island, and orchard lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4395 identities would post 2350 proofs and burn roughly 24 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
